steps: Check & measure the chimney
Factory-built (7" min. ID) or masonry (6" x 8" min. ID) solid-fuel chimney, 10'–40' tall. Remove the cap; fireplace base to chimney top, minus insert height, is the liner length.

The insert goes into a solid fuel masonry or factory-built non-combustible fireplace installed to national, provincial, state and local building codes. Any chimney clean-outs must fit properly.

  1. Remove and discard the existing chimney cap.
  2. With one person at the fireplace opening and one at the top of the chimney, measure from the fireplace base to the top of the chimney.
  3. Subtract the insert height. The result is the total length of co-linear flexible aluminum pipe needed; if using Kozy Heat #816, cut to length.

Where the chimney no longer terminates through the roof line, a co-linear to co-axial adapter may be installed where it ends (see Sections 4.2 and 6.3).
Prepare the fireplace
Verify the chimney is non-combustible, clean and in good working order; block the damper fully open or remove it. Plan the gas line (left side) and power, and attach the conversion warning label.

• Clean the chimney and fireplace to keep creosote odor out of the home.
  • Refractory, glass doors, screen rails, screen mesh and log grates may be removed. Removed parts must be re-installable if the insert is ever removed; removing rivets or screws is acceptable.
  • Confirm combustible mantel and sidewall clearances meet Section 8.1 (p. 27).
  • No gas access hole in a factory-built fireplace? Drill one 1½" (37.5 mm) or less through the lower sides or bottom of the firebox; plug it with non-combustible insulation once the line is in. Into minimum opening dimensions, the gas line may have to be run after placement.
  • Provide electrical power; the outlet box location is in Figure 2.1.
  • Mechanically attach the conversion warning label to the bottom of the existing firebox, where it will be visible if the insert is removed.
  • Outdoor covered fireplace installs: operation approved from 40°F to 110°F; overhang rules and black painted safety barriers on p. 24.
Attach liners to the cap

With #816 / #816-CAP: intake pipe over intake collar (A), exhaust pipe over exhaust collar (B) into high-temperature sealant, (3) self-tapping screws each. Mark the exhaust end; exhaust goes on the right.

The exhaust and combustion-air pipes must go on their correct collars at both the termination cap and the insert's vent adapter. The insert's exhaust collar is on the right side, so install the cap with its exhaust collar on the right.

  1. Measure the total chimney length; extend the pipes carefully and cut to length.
  2. Slide the combustion air intake pipe over intake collar (A); secure with (3) self-tapping screws (not provided).
  3. Bead high-temperature sealant around the base of exhaust collar (B), slide the exhaust pipe over the collar into the sealant and secure with (3) self-tapping screws. Mark the opposite end of the exhaust pipe.

Maximum horizontal run 24" (609mm). Avoid tight bends that can abrade or damage the flexible pipes.

Note: pp. 19–20 say horizontal vent runs need a 1" (25mm) rise per 12" (305mm) run; the troubleshooting chart on p. 51 says a 1/4" (6mm) rise per 12" (305mm) is required.
Run the liners
Slide the vent adapter back out of the channels on top of the insert. Feed both 3" x 3" pipes down the chimney, seal the cap to the chimney top, then pull both pipes into the firebox.

• Offsets in the chimney: put a weighted rope around each pipe end to guide it. Never tie one rope around both pipes.
  • To prevent cold air drafts, insulating the pipes and chimney with unfaced insulation listed non-combustible per ASTM E 136 is recommended. Optional: wrap the first 3' (914mm) below the cap before lowering (secure with wire), and fill between the pipes and chimney to cut heat loss.
  • Secure the termination cap with a liberal bead of sealant (not provided) around the top of the chimney.
Connect the vent adapter
Exhaust pipe inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', intake pipe over the intake collar: sealant and (3) ½" self-tapping screws each, then more sealant for an airtight joint.

1. Place the vent adapter in the existing fireplace opening.
  2. Exhaust: bead of sealant around the pipe, slide it inside the collar marked 'Exhaust', secure with (3) ½" (13mm) self-tapping screws, seal around the joint.
  3. Intake: liberal bead of sealant around the adapter's intake collar, slide the combustion intake pipe over it, secure with (3) ½" (13mm) self-tapping screws, seal around the joint.
  4. Visually check both connections.
Set & secure the insert
Slide it in until the top channels align with the adapter, draw the adapter forward with the pull rod and latch tool until seated, fix with (2) ½" screws, then level.

1. Slide the insert into the opening until the channels on top align with the vent adapter.
  2. Insert the pull rod through the access slot on top and hook the latch tool through the hole in the rod. Push the insert in while pulling the adapter forward until seated.
  3. Secure the adapter through the top slots with (2) ½" (13mm) sheet metal screws (components packet).
  4. Push the pull rod back to its starting position with the latch tool, remove the tool and verify the vent connection.
  5. If needed, level with the leveling bolts (components packet) threaded into the nuts at the bottom, 2 each side.

The insert must sit on a level surface able to support it and the venting (p. 12).
Gas line + leak test
Built for natural gas; convert with the kit for propane. A ½" tee handle shut-off valve and flexible connector go to the ½" control valve inlet; leak-test every connection with soapy water.

• Gas line by a qualified person to local codes, or ANSI Z223.1 if none; in Massachusetts, a licensed plumber or gas fitter.
  • Propane conversion follows the kit's instructions (LCK-NK29-S, p. 55) and ANSI Z223.1 / provincial requirements. Convert before installing light kits, panels or the log set.
  • Run the line preferably through the left gas line hole; the access hole cover can be repositioned for the back with its (4) screws. Don't route it where it would obstruct the fan.
  • Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve for supply-piping tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); for ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.
  • Check all connections, field or factory made, for leaks with soapy water (p. 34).
Note: p. 26 says the insert is equipped with a 3/8" (10 mm) x 18" (457 mm) flexible gas connector and manual shut-off valve; the parts list on p. 55 shows a 24" Flex Gas Line (700-224B) and a 24" Black 3/8" Gas Line (700-382B), and its only 18" part is the valve-to-burner-orifice flex tube (700-225F).
Bulbs, panels, logs & trim
Convert to propane first if needed. Fit the ember bed bulbs, the refractory or black glass panels, then the required log set; mount the shroud and hang the safety barrier.

• Bulbs (p. 31): disconnect power. The front bottom light kit takes (5) halogen bulbs from the components packet; the back bottom and top kits come with bulbs installed. Never touch bulbs with bare hands; use a soft cloth.
  • Panels (pp. 32–33): NK29-CB900, NK29-L900, NK29-BB900 or NK29-HB900 refractory, or NK29-BG900 black glass with 16-gauge backer plates. The left and right burners come out for this.
  • Log set (p. 34): one of the traditional or birch log sets is required; follow the log set's own instructions. Panels and ember bed bulbs go in first.
  • Shroud (p. 35): align the leg holes with the mounting nuts on each side and secure with (4) Phillips truss head screws. Trim must not seal the existing fireplace's ventilation or draft relief openings.
  • Safety barrier (p. 35): align the tabs on its back with the (4) slots on the glass frame (2 each side), raise slightly and let the tabs drop into place.
Initialize the controls
Rocker switch OFF, (4) AA in the backup holder, (3) AAA in the remote, then AC power. Clear the firebox, press the sync button (3 beeps), and within 5 seconds the remote's ON/OFF.

1. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox.
  2. Lift the safety barrier screen out of its slots to reach the ON/OFF rocker switch and remote sync button on the left side.
  3. Press the sync button: the IFC module beeps (3) times and lights an amber LED, ready to synchronize.
  4. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps confirm the transmitter's code is accepted, and the pilot lights.
  5. Press ON/OFF again; the pilot goes out, confirming the command. The control system is initialized.
  6. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation and reinstall the barrier screen.

These steps start the pilot in manual mode, where the igniter sparks repeatedly and the pilot lights if gas is supplied. Select IPI or CPI with the system off (p. 43).
Pressure test & flame check

Check inlet pressure at the IN tap and manifold pressure at the OUT tap (Tables 12.1 and 12.2). Re-seal each tap: turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the hose, tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure. Then watch the flame: blue at first, turning yellow over the first 15 minutes.

Venturi, NG (factory)Left 1/8" (3mm) · Right 1/8" (3mm) · Rear 5/8" (16mm)
Venturi, LP (factory)Left 3/8" (10mm) · Right 3/8" (10mm) · Rear 5/8" (16mm)
Intake restrictorNG 1/4" open · LP 1/2" open
  • Dark, orange flame with black tips: venturi closed too far, open slightly.
  • Short, blue flames: venturi open too far, close slightly.
  • Lifting (ghosting) flames: gas pressure too high and/or venturi closed too far; check manometer settings and/or open the venturi slightly.

Venturi adjustment is for a qualified service technician, in slight increments, with the unit cooled: remove the safety barrier, glass frame, glass media, lava rock (if installed) and media tray, loosen the venturi screw, adjust, re-tighten (p. 48). The air intake restrictor adjusts by loosening its two screws (p. 49).

panels.title: Pilot won't light
items: Power interrupted or disconnected → restore power or use battery backup
Wiring disconnection → on battery backup, check the batteries are charged; check connections against the wiring schematic
Gas supply turned off → check shut-off valves; there may be more than one between appliance and main line

panels.title: Pilot won't stay lit
items: No propane in tank → check the tank, refill
Low gas pressure (bent line, too narrow a pipe, low line pressure) → consult a plumber or gas supplier
Pilot not contacting the flame rectification sensor → pilot must envelop the top of the sensor and reach the burner
Pilot adjustment screw not sealed → seal it; don't over-tighten

panels.title: Main burner won't light
items: Rocker switch in OFF → switch to ON
Gas off or low → check for multiple shut-offs; check the propane tank
Wiring disconnected or wrong → check against Figure 10.1 wiring schematic
Pilot flame misdirected → direct it to ignite the burner
Remote / no call for heat → replace batteries; remote ON, thermostat operation OFF

panels.title: Pilot & burner go out in operation
items: No propane in tank → check the tank, refill
Glass assembly installed incorrectly → see 9.1 Glass Assembly
Vent cap installed incorrectly or blocked → adjust; remove debris
Exhaust pipe leaking back into firebox → check for leaks, repair
Improper horizontal vent pitch → p. 51 calls for a 1/4" rise per 12" of travel; pp. 19–20 call for a 1" rise per 12" run

codes: Below 4V; IFC double-beeps on ON/OFF and accepts no commands until the AA batteries are replaced
Both ignition attempts failed; verify gas is on and sensor isn't shorted, reset, or re-initialize per 11.2

light.title: Turning on the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself with an electric spark. You don't need a match or a gas knob, just the remote.

  1. With the fireplace off, press ON/OFF on the remote. The fireplace answers with one beep.
  2. About 4 seconds later it starts sparking at the pilot. The pilot flame then lights the burner.
  3. Once it's lit, set the flame height with the arrow keys.

If it doesn't light

It tries twice: about 60 seconds of sparking, a pause of about 35 seconds, then 60 seconds more. If the pilot still hasn't lit, it locks out and a red light blinks 3 times, over and over. To reset, press ON/OFF to turn it off, wait about 2 seconds and press it again. If it keeps happening, call a qualified technician.

No remote?

Lift the safety screen up and out to reach the rocker switch and sync button on the left side. Set the switch to OFF, hold the sync button until it beeps 3 times and an amber light comes on, then press it again within 5 seconds. The pilot lights, and the rocker switch now turns the burner on (high flame only) and off.

First fire: when the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue and gradually turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, have a qualified service technician check the burner air setting.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote runs on 3 AAA batteries and is paired with the fireplace during setup. One beep from the fireplace confirms a command.

Flame height

There are 6 flame levels. With the fireplace on, each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one level, all the way to off. Each press of the up arrow raises it one step. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow relights it on high.

Thermostat

  • Room thermostat: press the thermostat key. The screen shows a temperature bulb graphic, the room temperature and the set temperature. Use the arrows to pick the temperature you want.
  • Smart thermostat: press the thermostat key until “SMART” appears. It adjusts the flame height from the set and actual room temperatures, and turns the flame down when the room reaches the set point. While it's on, you can't change the flame by hand.

Handy extras

  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together to lock or unlock the keys, so the fireplace can't be run unsupervised. A lock icon shows while it's on.
  • °F or °C: with the fireplace off, press the thermostat and Mode keys together.
  • Low batteries: a battery icon appears on the screen before the power runs out, and goes away when you replace them.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
Your fireplace runs on 120-volt house power. A battery backup on the control module keeps it working when the power goes out.

Backup pack (control module)4 × AA, not included · 6 volt
Remote3 × AAA, included

During an outage

The burner and the flame height adjustment still work on the backup batteries. The fan and the accent lights don't.

When the backup batteries get low

The fireplace gives a low double beep when you press ON/OFF, and a red light blinks once at intervals. After that it won't accept any commands until you replace the batteries. Once new ones are in, it beeps once as soon as it has power.

How long the batteries last depends on things like their quality and how many times the fireplace lights.

Remote not responding? Low batteries in the remote or in the backup pack are the first thing to check.

sounds.title: What that beep or blink means
sounds.html:
Beeps

  • One beep: the fireplace received your remote command.
  • A low double beep when you press ON/OFF: the backup batteries are low. Replace them; it won't take commands until you do.
  • 3 beeps and an amber light: it's ready to pair with a remote after the sync button was pressed.

A blinking red light

  • 1 blink, repeating: backup batteries low.
  • 2 blinks: pilot flame problem. Contact your dealer.
  • 3 blinks: it locked out after two failed tries to light. See “Turn on the fireplace” for the reset.

It switched off by itself

When the pilot has stayed lit, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds within 24 hours to run a safety check, then repeats your last command. In CPI mode, the pilot also goes out after 7 days in a row without the main burner lighting. Both are built-in safety features.

Ticks and creaks

Some minor expansion, contraction or movement of parts that makes noise is normal, not a defect.

off.title: Turning it off & pilot modes
off.html:
With the fireplace on, press ON/OFF on the remote. You'll hear one beep, the main burner goes out, and the remote's screen shows only the room temperature.

Why the pilot may stay lit

The fireplace has two pilot modes:

  • IPI (intermittent pilot): the pilot is sparked alight each time the fireplace starts. No snowflake icon shows while it's on.
  • CPI (continuous pilot): a standing pilot stays lit. It keeps the firebox warm and sets up a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less airflow disruption. A snowflake icon shows on the screen.

Switch modes

  1. With the fireplace off, press Mode to step to the CPI icon.
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. One beep confirms it.

In CPI, if the main burner doesn't light for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns off by itself. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.

Pilot won't go out? The system is set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

fan.title: Fan & lights
fan.html:
Fan

The fan has 6 speeds. Press Mode until the fan icon shows, then use the arrows to turn it on or off or change the speed.

  • Thermostat mode: the fan waits 5 minutes after the fireplace lights so heat can build, and keeps running for about 12 minutes after it turns off.
  • Manual mode: the fan runs at its previous setting, with no delay starting or stopping.

Top accent light

It has 6 brightness levels. Press Mode until the light icon shows, then use the arrows.

Ember bed light

Press Mode until the AUX icon shows. The up arrow turns it on and the down arrow turns it off. To change its brightness, lift the safety screen up and out of its slots and turn the dimmer knob on the left side of the firebox: clockwise is brighter, counterclockwise is dimmer. Put the screen back when you're done.

The fan and lights don't run on battery backup, so they stay off in a power outage. The bulbs are halogen: never touch one with bare hands, use a soft cloth.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Cleaning the glass is listed as a yearly homeowner job. Do it only when the fireplace is cool: never remove or clean the glass while it's hot.

  1. Clear a flat, stable surface big enough for the glass assembly.
  2. Lift the safety screen up and out of its slots.
  3. With the glass latch tool from the components packet, pull the 2 spring-loaded latches at the bottom out and up. Lift the glass assembly up and off the 2 tabs at the top.
  4. Clean it with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  5. To refit, set the slots at the top over the tabs, lower the bottom into place, then use the latch tool to pull the latches out and down over the latch tabs.
  6. Put the safety screen back.
Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, or without the safety screen. Avoid striking or slamming the glass. Damaged glass should be replaced by a licensed or qualified service person, as a complete assembly from Hussong Mfg.

safety.title: Safety around the fireplace
safety.html:
• The glass gets hot. The safety barrier supplied with the fireplace reduces the risk of burns and must be in place to protect children and other at-risk people.
  • If the barrier is damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace (Prairie NK29-PSF, Arched Mission NK29A-MSF or Rectangular NK29-RSF).
  • Any screen, guard or barrier taken off for service goes back on before you use the fireplace.
  • Because of the high surface temperatures, keep it out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies. Keep the area clear of anything combustible, gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.
  • Don't run it with the glass removed, cracked or broken.
  • Use the remote's key lock to stop unsupervised use.
After a flood or leak: don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician right away to inspect it and replace any part of the control system and gas control that was under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have the fireplace inspected before use and at least once a year by a professional service person. Lint from carpeting or bedding can mean it needs cleaning more often: the control compartments, burners and air passages have to stay clean.

What the yearly service covers

  • Firebox: vacuumed, and the glass latches checked to move freely with spring tension.
  • Fan: disconnected and vacuumed. Its bearings are sealed and need no oiling.
  • Vent system: the vent and its cap checked for soot or blockage.
  • Glass: cleaned and checked for cracks, scratches and nicks.
  • Burner and pilot: vacuumed, gas connections leak-checked, ignition and the flame safety system tested, and the flame watched: it should be steady, not lifting or floating.

Your part

Clean the glass once a year (see “Clean the glass”), and keep the area around the fireplace clear of combustible materials, gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s Limited Lifetime Warranty covers the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship.

30 days · parts and laborPaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts and laborAll parts and material except the 30-day items
Years 2 through lifetime · parts onlyFirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shields, front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory firebox liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed only to an authorized dealer. If you spot a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days. There's nothing to mail in: keep your proof of purchase with the serial number and model.

What voids or limits it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual
  • The serial number or testing label removed, or the fireplace altered or tampered with
  • Submersion in water, or long periods of dampness or condensation
  • It can't be transferred: it's for the original purchaser only
This is a summary. The full terms and exclusions are in the manual.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
NG minimum5" WC (1.25 kPa)
NG recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
NG maximum10" WC (2.49 kPa)
LP min / max12" / 13" WC (2.99 / 3.24 kPa)

Test at the valve's IN tap (A) with a manometer on a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose, pilot and burner lit, and all other gas appliances in the house on or at full capacity. Too high or too low: contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician adjusts incoming pressure. Then re-seal the tap: turn off burner and pilot, disconnect the hose, tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten). Relight pilot and burner, then reattach the manometer to tap IN (A) to verify the tap is completely sealed: it should read no pressure.

Disconnect the appliance and its valve from the supply piping for tests above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at ½ psi or less, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
NG low / high1.1" / 3.8" WC (0.27 / 0.95 kPa)
LP low / high2.9" / 11" WC (0.72 / 2.74 kPa)

Test at the OUT tap (B): light the pilot, attach the manometer with a 1/4" (6mm) I.D. hose, light the burner and read. Turn burner and pilot off, disconnect the manometer hose and re-tighten the tap clockwise, snug (don't over-tighten). Then attach the manometer to tap OUT (B) to verify it's completely sealed: it should read no pressure with pilot and burner on.

Valve: S.I.T. IPI gas valve (700-567 NG / 700-567-1 LP) with 50% turndown stepper motor (700-504 / 700-504-1).

review.notes: Pages 2, 4, 6 and 59 have no text beyond the footer, and p. 39 (11.0 Operating Instructions) has only its heading; they are probably image-only (safety warnings, any 'what to do if you smell gas' block and the lighting label are not in the text), so the guide has no gas-smell procedure. Appliance dimensions exist only as Figure 2.1 (p. 9), so the catalog's height/width/depth could not be checked; the manual text gives no efficiency, so the catalog's AFUE figures could not be checked. The catalog view_area is larger than the replacement glass the manual lists (Glass with Gasket 17-1/4" x 26-7/8", 701-023T, p. 56); worth checking. Catalog feature 'one-piece shroud required' vs the parts list, which also lists 4-piece blank shrouds (NK29-004, NK29-008, p. 56). Drawings not transcribed: termination clearances Table 4.1 / Figures 4.2-4.3 (p. 16), roof-pitch rows beyond 'flat to 6/12' (p. 15, pitch labels missing in text), mantel/hearth Figures 8.1-8.4 (pp. 27-29), restrictor plate (p. 49), correct flame appearance Figure 14.3 (p. 54). Minor: p. 22 calls the intake-collar screws 'provided' but the exhaust-collar screws 'not provided'; the #816 roll is printed 35' (10.97 m), and the metric figure does not match the feet; the LP rear orifice is printed '72' in the spec table (p. 8) and '#72' in the parts list (p. 55); the lockout reset is misnumbered 10.7.1 on p. 41.
